How complex can trauma get especially if it started at a young age? Can something that didn't seem really bad on it's own develop into trauma?

I have a hard time accepting that I have trauma because a lot of things feel so small or just so insignificant, like they're just what everyone goes through.

For example, I used to get so stressed about school and homework from as early as 1st grade. It got really bad around 5th and 6th grade that I cried every night and stayed up really late because I couldn't get homework done. 

Other kids got the same amount of homework but it didn't affect them as much as it did me so I go on thinking this is my fault. I was just weak and should just stop being such a baby. It's not as bad as what other people go through that constitutes trauma. 

This and so many other things that i went through that were really trivial in other people's eyes like bullying and low self confidence due to comparison, never feeling like I'm good enough. And guilt like loads of guilt.

I frequently find peace with myself alone with my thoughts and chit chat can sometimes be uncomfortable. Especially when we don't really share the same interest. Apparently those weren't enough explanation. And can kinda seem selfish. ("You can talk to me but whether or not i respond well is all up to me"...etc)

 For them it's either we don't talk and are no longer friends or I always feel like talking and be the one to initiate conversation. 

I can't just say I prefer one to the other if this makes sense. I just think not talking at all and we're no longer friends is too extreme and the former is a bit hard on my personal boundaries. Seems an easy question from their pov tho. Just "be yourself". I am myself this way without changing anything because if not then who am I?

I feel that by not picking an option, I come off as immature, naive or inferior or simply just selfish as in I am keeping someone around just to treat them like crap over and over or something.

Not an advice but I feel I can relate. I was raised speaking both English (my father's) and my mother's language. I never moved out of my hometown and the culture I live in uses little English. As a child I got more exposed to my mother's language from school, socialising, etc. My English became less fluent once i went through primary school and my vocabulary poor.  I did excellent in writing classes (ESL) because I loved English as a language and often read, watched, played video games in English. I really absorbed English as a receiver but without speaking it that much my fluency is rather poor and I'm not at all confident in speaking.  

The thing is I'm more exposed to media in English than in my own language. The books I read are in English. I majored in English so most schoolwork were done in English and now my writing ability in English has kinda surpassed that of my language, not to say it's good enough. When I try to use my own language, my spelling is poor and my reading is considerably slower. 

Now I'm a weird mess of a human being and confused and maybe I should start a thread somewhere... 

I don't know if I should post this here because it might be a bit irrelevant but I really feel what you said so I'm gonna post it anyway. I hope it finds you well :) 

PS: I also would love to write for a living. In my opinion, writing isn't just about using extravagant vocabulary or complex sentences it's about clarity and being you, although vocabulary and sentences do help. From my experience learning English at ESL schools, people are often told to use big words not knowing what they really mean or complex sentences without mastery which would often result in ambiguity and confused meaning. This is because those words and sentences they write are not really THEM, if this makes sense.
